en.title: The verbs faire and prendre
en.goal: Conjugate the irregular verbs faire and prendre in the present tense.

blocks.title: Faire: a verb with a thousand uses
blocks.body: Faire (to do / to make) is irregular and shows up in lots of fixed expressions — including the weather ones you've already seen, like il fait chaud and il fait froid.

blocks.title: Prendre: to take, to catch, to have
blocks.body: Prendre (to take / to catch) is used both for transportation, as you've already seen, and for ordering food or drink — it's a very versatile everyday verb.

blocks.title: A similar pattern
blocks.body: Notice that both verbs change their stem in the plural — faire goes from fais-/fais-/fait- in the singular to faisons/faites/font in the plural, and prendre doubles the "n" in ils/elles prennent. These irregularities are worth paying attention to.
